title: David's Prayer and Divine Testing
english: From these syllables, it is most clearly shown that the Lord became man; for his soul, the flesh having been laid in the tomb, was in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights, having risen with the flesh, having severed the soul from the body. It is said that the flesh tabernacled in hope because of the resurrection that is to come; for it was not dissolved, suffering any corruption, but having remained unharmed, it was joined again to the soul which was not abandoned to Hades. But if the destined soul, being separated from flesh, stands existing even in Hades, then it is clear that the rational souls of men are not being; for the rational soul, being separated from flesh, does not stand existing, nor does it go into Hades. But truly the soul of Jesus has experienced both; for it has become both in the place of human souls, and having become outside of the flesh, it lives and stands; it is indeed rational and of the same essence as the souls of men, just as the flesh, having come forth from Mary, is of the same essence as the flesh of men. Even if it seemed to have suffered because of the cross, it was not destroyed; the fact that both soul and flesh remained unharmed, having been joined together again, was demonstrated. Again, the holiness of God has not seen corruption, but is also the cause of the resurrection of the others, the dead; for having become the firstborn from the dead, he, our corruptible and mortal being, having clothed himself in incorruption, undergoes death together with the holy of God who has not seen corruption.

The incarnate Word of God, having risen from the dead, sings praises (Ps 15:11), in that he has become man without abandoning even his being as God, having revealed to him the paths leading to eternal life, so that he may be filled with perfect joy, filling the saints with all spiritual joy. His image is the face of God and the exact imprint of his hypostasis. And what follows the one who has walked the known paths of life, to have divine delight in the truth and wisdom of God's right hand? And this is the only-begotten Son of God. And since the delight in the right hand of God is found to be unsurpassed, it will be an end that is not sought by any other; for all things have come to pass not for the sake of another, but for its own sake (Ps 15:11).

Some people, acting with arrogance, judge the one praying as being of moderate character; no one would say, 'Hear, O Lord, my righteousness, and let my judgment come forth from your face' (Ps 16:3). But David, not being arrogant, while doing all the will of God, but desiring to be judged with goodness, prayed that his judgment might come forth from the divine face. 'Let my eyes see straightness' (Ps 16:3). One prays to see straightness with the eyes of a man, by which God judges, bringing the judgment forth from his own face; one prays to behold the virtue of straightness. If, however, he prays to see it, he does not yet possess it; thus he is advised not to be arrogant by the way he offers the prayer. These things regarding perfect virtue should be considered, if anyone ever becomes greater than those previously foretold.

And through these things, much boldness of the speaker is manifest (Ps 16:3). For if he says these things concerning God, he manifests much of his own purity; for the heart of everyone who endures in obscurity is tested, and he who is afflicted in everything is not distressed, but enduring until the end, he is proven righteous; such as Job, to whom God said: 'If perhaps I may prove you, you shall be more righteous than I' (Job 2:9). [Or: If it is possible that I may prove you, that you may appear righteous, in the testing of your heart by the Lord and being refined and no iniquity being found in you?]. It is worth following to see what is meant by 'I visited in the night' (Ps 16:3); and indeed, if he calls the state of those in obscurity 'night' because of the dimness and having nothing propitious, in which God, having visited him, left him proven and, having refined through afflictions, showed him clean from all iniquities. It is said, 'I visited in the night' (Ps 16:3) and not thus: because the hidden things of the heart are not manifest to anyone except to Him to whom it is said, 'You alone know the hearts of men'; it was named night, and even those things, although they are dark to others because of the inscrutable, to you, who tested me by visiting me in the night, have been revealed. To this, 'If I had considered iniquity in my heart, do not hear me, Lord' (Ps 16:3) is conjoined.
To declare the works of men and dispositions, even in word, is evil (Ps 16:4a). But what are these works, those about which the apostle writes: 'For where there is jealousy among you...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Protection of the Right Hand and Wings
english: Are you not men and walking according to man? The works of men happen to be a hindrance to speaking, and the failure to find [truth] in him, having been ignited by God through trials and those nearby (Ps 16:4b).

The paths bearing one toward virtue seem to be hard, having much roughness; for how is the path not hard, which commands the one being struck to a place beyond the jaws, and the rest of the hand to receive insult? In addition to this, a rough path seems to be one through which someone struggles toward death for the sake of the truth. And it is, through injuries, the most bitter of threats, of fire and iron and the assault of wild beasts, the completion of this; except even if these paths and those related to them are hard, they are guarded because of the words of the lips of the protecting God, and they are made smooth as if they were no longer something hard or heavy. For John indeed writes, 'And his commandments are not heavy' (1 John 5:3), and Jesus says to those hearing his words, 'My yoke is good and my burden is light' (Matt 11:30). For from much habituation and training, approaching without interruption, the heavy things appear most light, and the bitter and joyless things are made upright with much ease.

But the paths of the Lord and of his saints happen to be the keeping of the commandments (Ps 16:5a), rather the energies according to virtue, being shown to be smooth and even, having been developed from constantly suffering [toil] by those hurrying to reach their end; and their end is blessedness and the fulfillment of the promises. Let us therefore run according to them, so that we may find salvation, not wavering in our steps, that is to say, not stumbling. And if the Lord should prepare them in his paths, he says of one having obtained this request: 'I ran without lawlessness and directed myself, and I ran the path of your commandments' (Ps 16:6), and 'You have enlarged my heart' (Ps 16:7).

'I have cried out' (Ps 16:7) is to be heard spiritually; for it is not necessary to have cried out toward the invisible God with a loud voice, but with an attentive mind; this is the cry of the inner man. His mercies are wonderful upon those hoping in him, even if they have something more paradoxical regarding the mercies having become through favor, as the God inclining toward us hears the words of the voice.

Nothing else is our power, but the power descending through goodness to receive our words. For this, the eyes of the Lord shall be upon the righteous, and his eyes toward them for their prayer (Ps 16:8).

The right hand of God will be no other than his only-begotten Son, as was said a little earlier: 'Delight is at your right hand unto the end' (Ps 16:7). The devil and his angels, and with them sorcerers and evil men, stand against this, from whom the holy one desires to remain harmless, saying to God: 'Protect me from those standing at your right hand, according to the pupil of my eye, so that my mind may remain harmless; but also cover me in the shelter of your wings from the face of the impious who desire to surround me with misery' (Ps 16:8). It is possible to call the impious and those opposing the right hand of God in various ways, according to the underlying subject. But the voice 'Protect me as the pupil of the eye' does not belong to everyone, but only to the one having been enlightened according to the soul, having the eyes of the heart enlightened. And 'In the shelter of your wings you will cover me' is to be understood spiritually; for the covering powers of God are called his wings, through which he covers and for the sake of good cheer protects the one beseeching to be rescued from the impious who are planning misery against him. For indeed, there are certain invisible enemies making misery for those being caught by them, by bringing them under sin.

The wild and raw [nature] of those standing against signifies, by saying, that his soul is being enclosed by his enemies who have shut their canopy because of the striving toward matter (Ps 16:9). For the others, through [their] lusts, are material and fleshy, having been overcome by sin, and they are being shut out from much good cheer and luxury, just as wheat and oil used to be filled. Therefore, the Ally was blocked from their canopy; therefore also their mouths speak pride, not steadily bearing anything friendly or appropriate. For indeed, the enemies, casting out from much arrogance, surround the one saying these things in order to harm and destroy the one who has become sheltered within. For they do not seek anything useful or good, since having become transgressors of divine laws through the...

title: The Deception of the Unworthy and the Vision of Glory
english: That their eyes are set upon the earth, turning aside and becoming lawless; for this is shown by having set their eyes upon the earth, wanting to observe the passing things and thinking of earthly things, turning aside from not wanting to walk the straight way, but being tossed about by crooked paths. For, they say, those abandoning the straight ways of going, they go in ways of darkness, whose ways are crooked and winding. Not indeed they set their eyes upon the earth, but those bearing the image of the heavenly are setting their eyes upon heaven in order to straighten the straight way that leads up to the heavens (Ps 16:13-14a).

Since you are long-suffering, that you might sleep, you do not receive justice from them who were cutting [me] murderously, Arise therefore, O Lord, that you might cause them to be overshadowed (Ps 16:13). For they will understand having suffered this, so that not always running toward evil they might increase their destruction; for surrounding my soul and doing other things, if not prevented, they harm it most greatly. Therefore overshadow them, so that they may no longer be able against me, you having rescued my soul from each one being such and therefore being named ungodly; for rescue my soul from the ungodly (Ps 16:14). He will take his sword from their hands; for they received it given unrighteously. And they take [it] from them not using it as is necessary. Therefore also in the earth they are few, that is to say, they are cheapened. For those becoming about material and worthless things, striving for them, cast away from the soul its dignity and the wealth it possesses, unless they set the material before them. Therefore also they are not called as in the [unspecified]... Thy rod to those who are not (Ps 16:14b-15).

Of those agreeing upon evil and being of one mind, the division of life is useful; for having set to do evil, being of one mind, they cast [it] away, becoming incomplete, having rebelled against them, as it has happened regarding the building of a tower and a city upon evil for themselves; for God, benefiting them, was holding their tongues together, so that they might no longer know anything said by their neighbors, so that the [unspecified]...

An ignorance, having taken hold, prepares them to turn back upon themselves, showing their purpose to be incomplete. This is what is made manifest in 'They are divided in their lives' and 'Their bellies were filled with your hidden things' (Ps 16:15). For the things unworthy of God's remembrance are hidden, whereas He leaves all the remnants to the infants after their bellies have been filled. What is unworthy of God's things that they seize upon is shown by Cain (for he went out from the presence of God [Gen 4:16]) and by those who do not remain lawful before your eyes. These, having become far from God, have been overwhelmed, and the remnants are left to their infants, having been gorged on filth. For among all those who corrupt, those who harm themselves and become a harm to others are more severe, which is shown by 'And he left the remnants to his infants.' For it is not possible to deceive those who truly are; therefore it is written concerning them: 'Because they wronged the infants, they shall be slain, and the scrutiny shall condemn the ungodly' (Ps 109:8). A scripture is brought forward: 'The sons were gorged; through the sons they ate filth.' Having been divided in their lives, they ate a manifold harm. For not only they, but also their infants were satiated with the hidden things of God.

They indeed are not, he says, as it is said, 'But I shall be seen in righteousness before your face' (Ps 16:15); for the virtue of the hidden ones from you is not like their wickedness. And those, being self-willed and thinking they are full of all things, having nothing, it seems they were sent to be gorged; but I, knowing in part, shall be satiated then, when your glory shall be seen standing according to the coming perfection, to face a Person face to face. It is possible to receive the glory of God when the Only-begotten Son is seen, as it is written: 'All flesh shall see his salvation, and the glory of the Lord shall be seen' (Luke 2:30). This is fulfilled in this, that we might behold the glory of the Son, a glory as the Only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. And they were counted among the enemies from whom he was rescued, and they are invisible differences. And the phenomena shall be spoken against each word. To the end.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
